extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and informed readers interested in composing or evaluating literary 'Romances' (Hawthorne/19th-century style)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing a literary 'Romance' (as Hawthorne defines it): how to use imaginative latitude, handle the marvelous, integrate moral purpose, and balance historical fact with invention while preserving emotional truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance vs. Novel: latitude and fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: When a writer calls his work a Romance, it need hardly be observed that he wishes to claim a certain latitude, both as to its fashion and material, which he would not have felt himself entitled to assume had he professed to be writing a Novel. The latter form of composition is presumed to aim at a very minute fidelity, not merely to the possible, but to the probable and ordinary course of man's experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Romance is permitted broader imaginative freedoms than a Novel — it may present truth under circumstances of the writer's own choosing — but it remains a work of art and must 'rigidly subject itself to laws.' Choose the Romance form when you need imaginative latitude, but be aware that the Novel expectation is strict fidelity to everyday probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Marvelous: sparing, flavor-like application
rubrics_metrics.description: He will be wise, no doubt, to make a very moderate use of the privileges here stated, and, especially, to mingle the Marvelous rather as a slight, delicate, and evanescent flavor, than as any portion of the actual substance of the dish offered to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate marvels or supernatural elements lightly and as atmospheric seasoning, not as the main substance of the story; avoid overreliance on the marvelous to carry the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to truth of the human heart
rubrics_metrics.description: While, as a work of art, it must rigidly subject itself to laws, and while it sins unpardonably so far as it may swerve aside from the truth of the human heart...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of imaginative liberties, ensure psychological and emotional verisimilitude — characters' motives and emotions must feel true even within invented circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view: connect bygone time with the present
rubrics_metrics.description: The point of view in which this tale comes under the Romantic definition lies in the attempt to connect a bygone time with the very present that is flitting away from us. It is a legend prolonging itself, from an epoch now gray in the distance, down into our own broad daylight, and bringing along with it some of its legendary mist...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrative perspective and atmosphere to fuse past and present — allow historical/legendary elements to linger in the contemporary setting to achieve a picturesque, evocative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral purpose: avoid didactic bluntness
rubrics_metrics.description: Many writers lay very great stress upon some definite moral purpose... the author has considered it hardly worth his while, therefore, relentlessly to impale the story with its moral as with an iron rod,—or, rather, as by sticking a pin through a butterfly,—thus at once depriving it of life, and causing it to stiffen in an ungainly and unnatural attitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the work has a moral theme, render it subtly through artful development rather than explicit preaching; high truths should emerge organically from the narrative rather than be forcibly imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assigning actual locality or directly portraying real communities
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader may perhaps choose to assign an actual locality to the imaginary events of this narrative... it exposes the romance to an inflexible and exceedingly dangerous species of criticism, by bringing his fancy-pictures almost into positive contact with the realities of the moment. It has been no part of his object, however, to describe local manners...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep fictional events and settings sufficiently detached from identifiable real places or social portraits to prevent misinterpretation or offense; present the tale as imagined rather than documentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters as authorial creations, not direct stand-ins for real persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The personages of the tale—though they give themselves out to be of ancient stability and considerable prominence—are really of the author’s own making... their virtues can shed no lustre, nor their defects redound, in the remotest degree, to the discredit of the venerable town of which they profess to be inhabitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct characters as invented entities so their traits do not reflect or injure real communities or individuals; disclaim or fictionalize resemblances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base fiction on particular facts but rearrange them to serve artistic purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Since research has disclosed the manner in which the romance is interwoven with incidents from the history of the Hawthorne family... such resemblances as these between sundry elements in the work of Hawthorne’s fancy and details of reality are only fragmentary, and are rearranged to suit the author’s purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw inspiration from historical or familial facts, but feel free to select, fragment, and rearrange details to serve narrative aims rather than attempting literal reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match form to material: use Romance's liberties for humble textures
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative, it may be, is woven of so humble a texture as to require this advantage, and, at the same time, to render it the more difficult of attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When your subject matter or material is modest or limited, using the Romance form's imaginative latitude can help elevate the narrative — but doing so well is challenging and demands careful art.
